sonnet.problem: The story card says the LORD calls Esau's descendants Israel's brothers and jokes that this is 'a family reunion'. That gives away the answer to the later true/false card 5, which asks whether the LORD tells Israel to treat them as enemies (the answer is False).
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The right answer ('That generation of fighting men had all died') is much longer and more Bible-sounding than the two wrong answers ('Moab opened its border', 'The people found the road'), so it stands out.
sonnet.rule: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

sonnet.problem: The card tells the death of the whole generation of fighting men ('When all those fighting men have died') and then adds a joke about the thirty-eight-year wait and putting an apron on. A card that tells death should carry no joke.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: In all three stops, the true/false cards follow the same order: a False card first, then a True card (Stop 1 cards 5 and 12, Stop 2 cards 2 and 8, Stop 3 cards 3 and 7). This is a set pattern repeated from stop to stop.
sonnet.rule: In a stop with 2 or more, at least one answer is True and at least one is False, in no set pattern.
